pair bonding depends on a receptor that prairie voles lack
the related species forms pairs but does so more slowly

questions.explanation: The comparison isolates receptor location as the difference between a pair-forming and a non-pair-forming species.

distractor_rationales.B: Boosting oxytocin speeds pair formation rather than preventing it.
distractor_rationales.D: The related species is described as not forming pairs.
distractor_rationales.C: Prairie voles have the receptor; the difference is its distribution.

questions.stimulus: Concrete gains strength as cement reacts with water. Below about five degrees Celsius the reaction slows sharply, and if fresh concrete freezes, ice expands and cracks it permanently. Builders therefore add accelerators or insulate the forms in cold weather. These precautions suggest that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: concrete gains strength faster when it freezes
concrete placed in freezing weather needs protection until it has gained enough strength to resist damage
accelerators remove the need to insulate concrete in cold weather
concrete placed in cold weather never reaches full strength

questions.explanation: The harm occurs while the concrete is fresh and weak, so protection is needed until it can survive a freeze.

distractor_rationales.A: Freezing cracks fresh concrete, which is damage rather than strength gain.
distractor_rationales.C: Accelerators and insulation are listed as alternatives, so accelerators do not replace insulation.
distractor_rationales.D: The text describes slowed reaction and damage, not a permanent ceiling.

questions.stimulus: Wood buried in seabed sediment without oxygen is attacked only slowly by microbes. When erosion exposes the timbers, oxygen returns and decay accelerates. Conservators therefore rebury exposed wreck sites or cover them with sand. This practice implies that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: microbes cannot survive in seabed sediment at all
excavation is the only way to preserve a wreck permanently
leaving a wreck buried can protect it better than exposing it for study
oxygen slows the decay of waterlogged wood

questions.explanation: The reasoning follows the decay mechanism: if oxygen drives decay, then keeping oxygen out by reburial preserves the wood.

distractor_rationales.D: Oxygen returns with exposure and decay accelerates.
distractor_rationales.B: The text describes reburial, not excavation, as a preservation measure.
distractor_rationales.A: The text says microbes attack slowly without oxygen, not that they are absent.

questions.stimulus: Bats deposit guano in caves, and insects and fungi break it down. Isotope analysis of guano layers shows shifts that match changes in the surrounding vegetation, and a core from a cave floor preserves a sequence of such layers thousands of years deep. Investigators therefore use guano cores to ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: show that bats prefer guano from a single plant species
reconstruct how the vegetation around a cave changed over time
measure the current population of bats in the cave
date the formation of the cave itself

questions.explanation: Because guano isotopes track vegetation and the core preserves layers in order, the core is a dated environmental archive.

distractor_rationales.C: A layer sequence records the past, not a present count.
distractor_rationales.D: The layers date accumulation, not the origin of the cave.
distractor_rationales.A: The text describes shifts in vegetation generally, not a single preferred species.

questions.stimulus: Green tea is heated soon after picking, which stops the oxidation that darkens leaves. Black tea is rolled and left to oxidise. The same cultivar can produce either tea depending on how it is handled after harvest. This comparison indicates that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: green tea comes from a different species than black tea
black tea is heated sooner after picking than green tea
oxidation is required to make green tea
the difference between green and black tea lies mainly in processing rather than in the plant

questions.explanation: The shared cultivar is the controlling fact: identical plants diverge because one is heated and the other oxidised.

distractor_rationales.A: The text says the same cultivar can produce either tea.
distractor_rationales.C: Heating stops oxidation, which is what makes green tea.
distractor_rationales.B: Black tea is left to oxidise; green tea is heated soon after picking.

questions.stimulus: Pack rats collect plant material and urinate on it, creating hard middens that preserve fragments for thousands of years. Middens in dry caves contain twigs from species that no longer grow nearby, and the layers can be dated. Researchers studying such middens can therefore infer ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: that the species found in the midden still grow nearby today
which plant species grew near the cave under earlier climate conditions
how many pack rats currently live in the cave
that the cave climate has remained unchanged for thousands of years

questions.explanation: Datable layers of preserved plants that are locally absent together support a picture of past vegetation and therefore past climate.

distractor_rationales.C: The middens record the past; they do not count present animals.
distractor_rationales.D: Species that no longer grow nearby imply a changed climate, not an unchanged one.
distractor_rationales.A: The text says those species no longer grow nearby.

questions.stimulus: Navigators in the Pacific learned to read swells reflected by islands and the flight paths of seabirds returning to land at dusk. A bird flying in a straight line at dusk is likely heading toward its roost, while birds that circle are likely still searching. A navigator who sees a steady line of birds can therefore ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: follow circling birds to reach an island faster
assume the birds have found no land and turn back
ignore the birds because they fly only during the day
use their direction of flight as a clue to where land lies

questions.explanation: A straight line at dusk signals a roost, so the flight direction points toward land that the navigator cannot yet see.

distractor_rationales.B: A steady line implies a destination, not a failure to find one.
distractor_rationales.A: Circling birds are described as still searching.
distractor_rationales.C: The observation is made at dusk, when the birds are flying.

questions.stimulus: Capacitance sensors estimate soil moisture from the dielectric properties of soil. Salinity changes those properties too, so a sensor reading in a saline soil reflects both water and dissolved salt. Readings from such soils must therefore be ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: discarded entirely, since no soil measurement is possible
interpreted as showing less water than is actually present in every case
used without adjustment because salinity has no effect on capacitance
corrected for salinity before they are treated as a measure of water content

questions.explanation: The confound is named explicitly, so the inference is a calibration step rather than a claim about which way the error runs.

distractor_rationales.C: The text says salinity changes the same properties the sensor reads.
distractor_rationales.A: The text calls for correction, not for abandoning measurement.
distractor_rationales.B: The direction of the error is not stated, so a universal over- or under-estimate cannot be inferred.

questions.stimulus: In a nineteenth-century maternity ward, the death rate from fever was higher among patients attended by physicians than among those attended by midwives. The physicians also performed autopsies before their ward rounds, while the midwives did not. An observer who noticed this pattern might reasonably conclude that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: midwives were better trained than physicians in every respect
something carried from the autopsy room may have contributed to the fever
autopsies were performed in order to treat the fever
the fever was caused by the patients' living conditions alone

questions.explanation: The one difference that tracks the death rate is the physicians' contact with autopsies, which points to transmission from that contact.

distractor_rationales.A: The comparison concerns fever deaths, not overall training.
distractor_rationales.D: Living conditions are not mentioned and cannot explain the difference between the two wards.
distractor_rationales.C: Autopsies are presented as preceding ward rounds, not as treatment.

questions.stimulus: Owls fly almost silently. Their flight feathers have a comb-like leading edge and a soft trailing fringe that break up the turbulent air flowing over the wing. In wind-tunnel tests, wings with these features produced less noise than smooth wings at the same speed. The feather structure therefore appears to ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: reduce the noise created by airflow over the wing
increase the speed at which the owl can fly
make the wing heavier and more rigid
produce a louder call for communication

questions.explanation: Because the test varies only the feather features at a fixed speed, the reduced noise can be attributed to the structure.

distractor_rationales.B: Speed is held constant in the comparison; noise is the measured difference.
distractor_rationales.C: The features are described as structural and soft, not as adding rigidity.
distractor_rationales.D: The passage concerns flight noise, not vocal calls.

questions.stimulus: Paper made from wood pulp contains lignin, which yellows and embrittles as it oxidises. Papers made from cotton rags lack lignin and remain flexible for centuries. Conservators who want to slow the deterioration of a wood-pulp document therefore usually ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: add lignin to the paper to strengthen it
replace the document with a cotton-rag copy and discard the original
store the document in bright light to stop oxidation
treat the paper to remove or neutralise the lignin and the acids it produces

questions.explanation: The contrast with lignin-free cotton paper identifies lignin as the agent of decay, which is what treatment would target.

distractor_rationales.A: Lignin is the cause of the yellowing and embrittlement.
distractor_rationales.C: Light accelerates oxidation rather than stopping it.
distractor_rationales.B: The question asks how to slow deterioration of the document, not how to replace it.

questions.stimulus: Salmon that return to spawn carry marine nitrogen into rivers. Trees along streams where salmon spawn contain measurably more of that nitrogen than trees along streams without salmon. This pattern suggests that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: the nitrogen in the trees comes from rainwater rather than the ocean
salmon avoid streams where trees grow densely
spawning salmon transfer nutrients from the ocean to the surrounding forest
trees along salmon streams absorb nitrogen only from the soil

questions.explanation: The marine signature appears only where salmon spawn, which supports a transfer from fish to forest.

distractor_rationales.D: The comparison turns on salmon presence, so the trees are receiving marine nitrogen.
distractor_rationales.B: No such avoidance is described, and the presence of salmon is what predicts the nitrogen.
distractor_rationales.A: The isotope signature is specifically marine.

questions.stimulus: Birds flying in a wind tunnel were filmed with tracer particles. As air speed increased, the birds shifted the angle of their wings, and the wake behind them changed from a single vortex to a pair of vortices. These observations indicate that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: the pattern of airflow behind a bird changes as its flight speed changes
tracer particles alter the way birds flap in a tunnel
birds produce the same wake at every speed
wing angle has no effect on the air moving over the wing

questions.explanation: Both the wing angle and the wake change together with speed, so the wake structure is speed-dependent.

distractor_rationales.C: The wake is described as changing from one vortex to a pair.
distractor_rationales.D: The birds shift wing angle as speed rises, alongside the wake change.
distractor_rationales.B: The particles are a visualisation method; the text does not suggest they change flight.

questions.stimulus: Salt marshes accumulate sediment and can rise as sea level rises, but only if the sediment supply keeps pace. Marshes behind dikes that block sediment often drown, while nearby marshes with open tidal channels keep their elevation. Managers seeking to keep a marsh above water therefore sometimes ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: remove all vegetation so that sediment can settle
restore tidal flow so sediment can reach the marsh surface
pump water out of the marsh to lower its surface
build higher dikes to hold back the sea

questions.explanation: The contrast between diked and open marshes points to sediment supply through tidal channels as the factor that lets a marsh keep up.

distractor_rationales.D: Dikes are the condition associated with drowning because they block sediment.
distractor_rationales.A: Vegetation is not described as blocking sediment.
distractor_rationales.C: Lowering the surface would worsen the problem the manager is trying to solve.

questions.stimulus: Roman fish sauce was made by salting fish and leaving the mixture in the sun for weeks. Enzymes and bacteria break the proteins into amino acids, including glutamate, which the human tongue detects as savoury. The sauce's distinctive taste therefore came from ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: whole fish that were never broken down
salt added at the end of the process
compounds produced as proteins broke down during fermentation
the absence of bacteria during curing

questions.explanation: The taste is attributed to glutamate released by protein breakdown, which is the fermentation step the text describes.

distractor_rationales.B: Salt is part of the curing mixture, not a flavour added at the end.
distractor_rationales.A: The proteins are broken into amino acids.
distractor_rationales.D: Bacteria are named as agents of the breakdown.

questions.stimulus: As coffee beans roast, acids are destroyed and new aromatic compounds form. A light roast retains more of the acids, while a dark roast contains more of the bitter compounds produced by heat. Two roasts of the same green beans therefore ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: taste identical because they began as the same beans
differ in flavour because the roasting process changes which compounds dominate
contain more acids as the roast gets darker
differ because dark beans come from a different plant species

questions.explanation: The same starting material plus different roasting produces different compounds, so the difference is processing rather than origin.

distractor_rationales.A: The passage explains that roasting creates and destroys different compounds.
distractor_rationales.D: The text contrasts light and dark roasts directly.
distractor_rationales.C: The text says acids are destroyed and a dark roast retains fewer.

questions.stimulus: Lightning in volcanic plumes occurs when ash particles collide and separate charge, much as ice crystals do in thunderstorms. Plumes with a larger ash load produce more lightning. Observers monitoring an eruption from a safe distance can therefore use lightning activity to ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: measure the temperature of the magma below
determine the chemical composition of the ash
predict exactly when the eruption will end
estimate how much ash the plume is carrying

questions.explanation: Because the charging mechanism scales with ash load, lightning gives an indirect measure of how much ash is present.

distractor_rationales.C: The text draws no connection between lightning and eruption duration.
distractor_rationales.A: The mechanism concerns ash collisions, not magma temperature.
distractor_rationales.B: The text relates lightning to the quantity of ash, not its chemistry.

questions.stimulus: Paper wasps chew wood fibres and build combs of hexagonal cells. The cells are open downward, and larvae hang inside them. Species that build in sheltered cavities have cells that open in various directions, while species that build in the open all have downward-facing cells. This contrast suggests that the downward orientation ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: helps the wasps find their way back to the nest
makes the comb easier to attach to a branch
is required for the larvae to breathe inside the cell
protects the brood from rain where the nest is exposed

questions.explanation: The difference tracks exposure: only open-air builders always point cells down, which is consistent with shedding rain.

distractor_rationales.B: Attachment is not discussed in the comparison.
distractor_rationales.C: No connection between orientation and respiration is given.
distractor_rationales.A: Navigation is not mentioned.

questions.stimulus: Trees form wide rings in wet years and narrow rings in dry years. A series of measured rings from a living tree can be matched to the pattern in an old roof beam, allowing the beam to be placed in the same sequence. Dendrochronologists can therefore use ring patterns to ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: date timbers by matching them to a known sequence of years
determine the species of a beam without examining its wood
show that every tree in a region has an identical ring sequence
measure the current rainfall in a forest

questions.explanation: The matched pattern places an undated beam against a dated sequence, which is the definition of cross-dating.

distractor_rationales.D: Ring widths record past conditions, not present rainfall.
distractor_rationales.B: Matching sequences dates wood; it does not identify species.
distractor_rationales.C: The method relies on matching patterns, not on identical sequences everywhere.

questions.stimulus: Dust settles on the solar panels of Mars rovers and reduces the power they collect. Gusts occasionally clear panels, and operators have learned to park a rover on a slope so that gravity helps loose dust slide off. This strategy suggests that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: rovers generate more power on flat ground than on slopes
dust on Mars is permanently fixed to panel surfaces
tilting a panel can help remove dust when wind alone is not enough
wind on Mars never clears dust from panels

questions.explanation: Combining occasional wind with a tilt that lets gravity move dust supports the idea that angle helps when wind is insufficient.

distractor_rationales.B: The text describes gusts clearing panels and a slope supplementing them.
distractor_rationales.A: The slope is chosen to shed dust, which implies a power benefit.
distractor_rationales.D: The text says gusts occasionally clear panels.

questions.stimulus: Some frogs secrete peptides on their skin that kill bacteria. Bacteria living on frog skin are often resistant to those same peptides, while bacteria from nearby ponds are not. This difference suggests that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: frogs absorb resistant bacteria from the pond to protect themselves
skin bacteria have evolved tolerance to the defenses of the frog they live on
pond bacteria are exposed to more frog peptides than skin bacteria
the frog's peptides are ineffective against all bacteria

questions.explanation: Resistance appears only in the community that lives with the peptides, which points to selection in that habitat.

distractor_rationales.D: The peptides are effective against pond bacteria.
distractor_rationales.C: Skin bacteria live in direct contact with the peptides.
distractor_rationales.A: The comparison shows resistance arising on the skin, not being acquired from the pond.

questions.stimulus: Ice accumulating on the leading edge of a wing disrupts smooth airflow and reduces lift. De-icing systems use heat or inflatable boots to break the ice away. After a de-icing cycle, lift returns to near its clean-wing value. These results indicate that the loss of lift was caused by ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: smooth airflow over the leading edge
permanent deformation of the wing structure
the weight of the de-icing equipment
the disruption of airflow by the ice, not by permanent damage to the wing

questions.explanation: Reversibility is the key signal: if removing the ice restores lift, the ice's interference with airflow caused the loss.

distractor_rationales.B: Lift returns after the ice is removed, so the wing itself is not permanently damaged.
distractor_rationales.C: Equipment weight is not measured or discussed.
distractor_rationales.A: Smooth airflow is the condition that restores lift.

questions.stimulus: Bamboo poles are strong for their weight and flex under wind loads. In some cities, scaffolding is still built from bamboo lashed with plastic strips rather than steel tube. Engineers note that bamboo scaffolds have survived typhoons that damaged rigid structures nearby. Bamboo's flexibility therefore appears to ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: help the structure absorb wind energy instead of resisting it rigidly
reduce the strength of the poles to below that of plastic
prevent the scaffold from moving at all in high wind
make the structure heavier than an equivalent steel frame

questions.explanation: The contrast with rigid structures that failed points to flexing as the mechanism that lets bamboo survive high winds.

distractor_rationales.D: The text says bamboo is strong for its weight.
distractor_rationales.C: Flexing is the opposite of not moving.
distractor_rationales.B: Plastic strips are the lashing, not a comparison of strength.

questions.stimulus: Tardigrades survive extreme drying by replacing water in their cells with a sugar that forms a glass-like solid. In this state, proteins keep their shape instead of unfolding. When water returns, the sugar dissolves and normal activity resumes. The sugar therefore functions to ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: hold proteins in a stable shape while water is absent
prevent water from ever returning to the cells
provide energy for the animal during drought
dissolve the proteins so they can be rebuilt later

questions.explanation: The glass-like solid is explicitly tied to preserving protein shape through desiccation.

distractor_rationales.C: No energy role is described.
distractor_rationales.B: Water returns and activity resumes.
distractor_rationales.D: Proteins keep their shape rather than dissolving.

questions.stimulus: Homing pigeons released from an unfamiliar site often circle before setting off. Their initial heading is more accurate when the sun is visible than when the sky is overcast. On overcast days, birds released from the same site take longer to depart and are more often lost. These observations suggest that pigeons ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: fly more accurately when the sky is overcast
use the sun as one cue for setting their initial direction
circle because they have already located home
navigate only by landmarks they memorised before release

questions.explanation: The sun's visibility changes accuracy at an unfamiliar site, which isolates it as a compass cue rather than a learned route.

distractor_rationales.D: An unfamiliar site rules out memorised landmarks as the only cue.
distractor_rationales.A: Accuracy is worse when the sky is overcast.
distractor_rationales.C: Circling precedes departure and is associated with uncertainty.

questions.stimulus: Slag from iron smelting contains iron in proportion to how efficiently the furnace ran. Heaps of slag at an excavated site therefore allow archaeologists to estimate how much ore was processed there, even when the furnaces themselves have not survived. The method depends on knowing ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: the number of workers employed at the site
the exact age of the slag heap
how much iron the slag holds relative to the ore that produced it
the price of iron at the time of smelting

questions.explanation: Turning slag quantity into an ore estimate requires a conversion factor, which is the iron content relative to the original ore.

distractor_rationales.B: Age does not affect the conversion from slag to ore.
distractor_rationales.A: Workforce size is not part of the calculation described.
distractor_rationales.D: Price is unrelated to the physical proportion of iron.

questions.stimulus: Diatoms have silica shells that preserve in lake sediment. Different species thrive at different nutrient levels, so the species present in a sediment layer reflect the water at the time the layer formed. A core spanning several centuries can therefore be used to ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: trace how nutrient levels in the lake changed over time
identify the age of the lake basin itself
show that all diatom species prefer the same conditions
measure the lake's current nutrient level directly

questions.explanation: Because species composition tracks nutrients and the core preserves layers in order, the core becomes a timeline of nutrient conditions.

distractor_rationales.D: A core records past layers rather than present water.
distractor_rationales.B: The layers date sediment, not the basin's origin.
distractor_rationales.C: The method depends on species differing in preference.

questions.stimulus: Dust on solar panels reduces the light reaching the cells. In dry regions, cleaning is limited by the availability of water, so operators wait longer between washes than they would elsewhere. In such regions, panel output is therefore expected to ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: decline faster between cleanings than in wetter regions
remain constant because water is scarce
be unaffected by dust because the air is dry
improve as dust accumulates on the glass

questions.explanation: Less frequent cleaning in dusty conditions means more accumulated dust, so output falls further between washes.

distractor_rationales.C: Dust reduces light regardless of humidity.
distractor_rationales.D: Accumulating dust blocks light rather than improving it.
distractor_rationales.B: Waiting longer between washes allows more dust to build up.

questions.stimulus: Some moths produce clicks that interfere with bat echolocation. When bats hunt clicking moths in a chamber, they capture fewer than when they hunt silent moths of the same size. The clicks therefore appear to ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: make the moths larger on echolocation displays
reduce the bats' ability to locate the moths
attract bats from a greater distance

questions.explanation: Holding size constant and varying only the clicks isolates the sound as the cause of the lower capture rate.

distractor_rationales.D: Attraction would raise capture, not lower it.
distractor_rationales.A: The comparison uses moths of the same size.
distractor_rationales.C: Accuracy falls when the moths click.

questions.stimulus: A nightingale's song has a whistle section and a trill section. Researchers recorded individually marked males throughout the night and compared the two sections across hours. Early in the night, males sang long whistle sections; later, the trills grew longer. The shift suggests that the song serves different functions at different hours, perhaps advertising territory first and attracting a mate later.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the structure of the text?

choices.text: It states a theory and then reports an experiment that rejects it.
It lists several competing explanations without choosing among them.
It compares two species and explains why one is more successful.
It describes a pattern observed over time and then offers an explanation for it.

questions.explanation: The first sentences report a measured change across the night; the last sentence interprets that change as a shift in function.

distractor_rationales.A: The explanation is supported, not rejected.
distractor_rationales.C: Only one species is discussed.
distractor_rationales.B: One explanation is advanced, not several left open.

questions.stimulus: Some plants attach oily packages to their seeds. Ants carry the seeds underground, eat the package and abandon the seed in a chamber. The plant gains burial in a moist, protected space, and the ant gains food. The relationship is a trade: the plant pays in oil and receives transport and shelter for its offspring.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the structure of the text?

choices.text: It compares two plants and argues that one is better adapted.
It presents a hypothesis and then describes an experiment that tests it.
It traces a sequence of events and then characterises the relationship between the two organisms.
It describes a problem and then proposes a technological solution.

questions.explanation: The passage narrates what happens to seed and ant, then names the exchange as a trade, which is its purpose.

distractor_rationales.B: No experiment is described.
distractor_rationales.A: Only one plant strategy is discussed.
distractor_rationales.D: No technology or problem-solving is involved.

questions.stimulus: Ancient harbour concrete has outlasted modern port cement exposed to the same waves. The difference is not the aggregate but the binder: Roman mixes included lumps of lime that never fully combined. Water reaching a crack dissolves calcium from those lumps and precipitates minerals that seal it. What looked like careless mixing is now understood as a self-repair system.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the structure of the text?

choices.text: It argues that modern cement is superior because it is more uniform.
It describes a manufacturing process in chronological order without evaluating it.
It poses a contrast, identifies its cause, and then revises the original interpretation of the material.
It compares two ancient sites and explains their different climates.

questions.explanation: The passage opens with a contrast, explains it through the lime lumps, and closes by reinterpreting those lumps as functional.

distractor_rationales.B: The text evaluates the material and explains a mechanism.
distractor_rationales.A: Modern cement is presented as the less durable comparison.
distractor_rationales.D: No two sites are compared.

questions.stimulus: The wing hinge of a flying insect is a set of elastic pads and hard plates. When a muscle pulls, the hinge stores energy and releases it at the end of each stroke. High-speed films show that the wing reverses direction before the muscle has finished contracting. The hinge, not the muscle alone, sets the rhythm of the stroke.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.text: To describe how to build a mechanical wing hinge
To explain how an anatomical structure contributes to the timing of insect flight
To argue that insect muscles are stronger than vertebrate muscles
To compare the flight speeds of several insect species

questions.explanation: The passage describes the hinge and uses film evidence to show that it, not just the muscle, times the wingbeat.

distractor_rationales.C: No comparison with vertebrates is made.
distractor_rationales.A: The text describes a natural structure, not a construction method.
distractor_rationales.D: Speeds are not compared.

questions.stimulus: Permafrost holds large stores of frozen organic matter. When it thaws, microbes begin to decompose that material and release carbon dioxide and methane. A decade-long monitoring study found that emissions rose fastest in the first years after thaw and then slowed as the easily decomposed material was used up. The study's authors caution that the slowdown may not hold if deeper layers continue to thaw.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the structure of the text?

choices.text: It compares two regions and explains why one thaws faster.
It states a policy recommendation and then reviews the evidence for it.
It describes a process, reports a finding, and ends with a limitation on that finding.
It presents a hypothesis that the reported study confirms without reservation.

questions.explanation: The text moves from mechanism to measurement to caveat, which is the shape of the whole passage.

distractor_rationales.B: No policy is recommended.
distractor_rationales.A: Regions are not compared.
distractor_rationales.D: The final sentence explicitly qualifies the finding.

questions.stimulus: Medieval scribes often left wide margins and filled them with small drawings. One explanation is decoration. Another is practical: parchment was expensive, and a copied text could be corrected or annotated only if space remained. Analysis of surviving manuscripts finds more marginal notes in texts used for teaching than in luxury copies, which supports the practical explanation.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the structure of the text?

choices.text: It reports a single explanation as established fact.
It argues that decoration was the only reason for wide margins.
It presents two explanations and then describes evidence favoring one.
It describes a technique and then explains how to reproduce it.

questions.explanation: The passage sets two possible reasons side by side and then uses the distribution of notes to prefer the practical one.

distractor_rationales.D: No reproduction method is given.
distractor_rationales.B: Decoration is one candidate explanation, not the sole one.
distractor_rationales.A: A second explanation is offered and tested.

questions.stimulus: Whale sharks are the largest fish, yet their movements are poorly known because they spend long periods offshore. Researchers fitted sharks with tags that record depth and light level; the light record estimates position from day length and solar angle. Tracks from tagged animals showed repeated visits to the same seamounts. The tags turned an elusive animal into a mapped one.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the structure of the text?

choices.text: It states a problem, explains a method used to address it, and reports a result.
It describes the anatomy of a whale shark in detail.
It compares two tagging technologies and recommends one.
It argues that whale sharks are more common than previously thought.

questions.explanation: The difficulty of studying an offshore animal, the light-and-depth tags, and the seamount tracks form a problem-method-result structure.

distractor_rationales.C: Only one tagging approach is described.
distractor_rationales.B: Anatomy is not the subject.
distractor_rationales.D: The finding concerns movement patterns, not abundance.

questions.stimulus: Cities are often warmer than the countryside around them. The difference comes from dark surfaces that absorb sunlight, from buildings that trap heat, and from the removal of vegetation that would otherwise cool the air. Measurements at night show the largest gap, because stored heat is released after sunset. The effect is therefore strongest when the sun is not shining.
questions.prompt: Which choice best explains why the text mentions night-time measurements?

choices.text: To describe how the urban heat island is measured rather than explained
To argue that vegetation has no effect on urban temperature
To show that the heat stored during the day continues to affect temperature after sunset
To prove that cities are cooler than the countryside at night

questions.explanation: The night-time maximum is used as evidence that surfaces store daytime heat and release it later.

distractor_rationales.D: The gap is largest at night, meaning cities stay warmer.
distractor_rationales.B: Vegetation is one of the causes named.
distractor_rationales.A: The measurements support an explanation of stored heat.

questions.stimulus: A termite mound stays close to a constant temperature even when the outside air swings widely. The mound's walls are porous, and its internal structure channels warm air upward and draws cooler air in from the base. Architects have copied the principle in buildings that rely on stack ventilation rather than air conditioning. The mound is the model; the building is the application.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the structure of the text?

choices.text: It describes a natural system without mentioning any human use.
It explains why termites cannot regulate the temperature of a mound.
It compares two building designs and argues that one is cheaper.
It describes how a natural system works and then shows how that principle has been applied.

questions.explanation: The passage explains the mound's ventilation and then names buildings that use the same stack principle.

distractor_rationales.C: Cost is not discussed.
distractor_rationales.A: The final sentences explicitly describe architectural application.
distractor_rationales.B: The mound is said to stay near constant temperature.

questions.stimulus: Light travels along a glass fibre by reflecting repeatedly from its walls. A fibre with a core of slightly higher refractive index than its cladding keeps the light inside even when the fibre bends. Medical instruments use bundles of such fibres to carry illumination in one direction and images back in the other. The same property that confines the light makes the bundle flexible enough to insert.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.text: To describe the manufacture of glass from raw materials
To compare glass fibres with copper wires for data transmission
To argue that fibre optics are unsuitable for medical instruments
To explain the optical property behind fibre bundles and how it enables a medical use

questions.explanation: The refractive-index difference is the principle, and the instrument bundle is the use drawn from it.

distractor_rationales.B: Data transmission is not discussed.
distractor_rationales.A: Manufacturing is not described.
distractor_rationales.C: The text presents a medical use as an application.

questions.stimulus: Ships carry ballast water to stay stable, and they discharge it in the next port. Organisms carried in that water can survive the voyage and establish in new waters. Regulations now require ships to treat ballast before release, using filtration, heat or ultraviolet light. The rules exist because a single discharge can move a species across an ocean.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the structure of the text?

choices.text: It explains why a practice is a problem and then describes the response to it.
It compares three treatment methods and identifies the cheapest.
It describes the history of ship design over several centuries.
It argues that ballast water is harmless to receiving ports.

questions.explanation: The practice, the ecological consequence, and the regulation form a problem-and-response structure.

distractor_rationales.C: No historical development is traced.
distractor_rationales.B: Costs are not compared.
distractor_rationales.D: The text says organisms can establish in new waters.

questions.stimulus: Fire leaves a scar in a tree's rings: the wood just under the bark is damaged, and later rings grow around the wound. By counting rings inward from the scar, researchers date the fire to the year it occurred. A survey of scars across a valley can then be assembled into a map of past fires, showing which years burned and how far the fires spread.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the structure of the text?

choices.text: It argues that fires are no longer a natural part of forests.
It compares two ways of dating fires and rejects one.
It explains a dating method and then describes what a collection of such dates can reveal.
It describes the effect of fire on soil chemistry.

questions.explanation: The scar-dating technique comes first, and the valley-scale map is the larger use built from many dated scars.

distractor_rationales.B: Only one method is presented.
distractor_rationales.D: Soil chemistry is not discussed.
distractor_rationales.A: No such argument is made.

questions.stimulus: Two related birds build very different nests. One weaves a hanging pouch with a narrow entrance; the other builds an open cup on a branch. The pouch builder lives where tree snakes are common, and the entrance is too small for the snake to pass. The cup builder lives where snakes are absent, and its open nest allows faster access for feeding.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the structure of the text?

choices.text: It describes one species and then rejects a theory about it.
It describes a single nest-building technique step by step.
It contrasts two behaviors and explains the contrast by their different environments.
It argues that open nests are always better than enclosed ones.

questions.explanation: The nest forms differ, and the difference is tied to the presence of snakes and the demands of feeding.

distractor_rationales.A: Two species are contrasted throughout.
distractor_rationales.D: No such ranking is offered; each nest suits its setting.
distractor_rationales.B: Two techniques are compared, not one sequenced.

questions.stimulus: Moths of several species hear ultrasound and fly away from it. Bats hunt by emitting ultrasound and listening for echoes. Researchers played recorded bat calls to moths on a screen and filmed their responses; most turned away within a fraction of a second. A control group exposed to a tone outside the bats' range showed no such response.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the structure of the text?

choices.text: It describes two competing theories and confirms both.
It describes the life cycle of a moth in chronological order.
It explains how bats produce ultrasound but not how moths respond.
It describes a behavior and reports an experiment that tests its function.

questions.explanation: The escape behavior and the playback experiment with a control together establish that the response is to bat calls.

distractor_rationales.A: A single explanation is tested rather than two theories confirmed.
distractor_rationales.C: Moth response is the focus of the experiment.
distractor_rationales.B: No life cycle is described.

questions.stimulus: Salt crystallising inside porous stone exerts pressure that can flake away the surface. Conservators can slow the damage by reducing the moisture that carries salt into the stone. In one treatment, a poultice draws dissolved salt out through the surface over weeks. The stone is not strengthened, but the source of the pressure is reduced.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the structure of the text?

choices.text: It compares two stones and argues that one is more porous.
It lists several causes of damage without discussing remedies.
It describes a treatment and then claims it strengthens the stone.
It explains a cause of damage and then describes a treatment that addresses that cause.

questions.explanation: The mechanism is salt pressure from moisture, and the poultice acts on that moisture rather than on the stone's strength.

distractor_rationales.A: Two stones are not compared.
distractor_rationales.C: The text says the stone is not strengthened.
distractor_rationales.B: One cause and one remedy are described.

questions.stimulus: Schools of fish move in coordinated patterns that look like a single animal turning. One model explains this by having each fish copy only its nearest neighbors. The model reproduces the turning patterns well. It fails, however, when a predator attacks: real schools spread apart faster than the model predicts, suggesting that fish also respond to more distant cues.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the structure of the text?

choices.text: It describes a model, notes its success, and then identifies a case it cannot explain.
It describes an experiment that measured the swimming speed of fish.
It argues that fish schools have no coordinated behavior at all.
It presents a model that explains every observed behavior.

questions.explanation: The passage gives the neighbor-copying model credit and then uses the predator response as a counterexample.

distractor_rationales.D: The final sentence names a case the model fails to explain.
distractor_rationales.B: Speed is not measured in the passage.
distractor_rationales.C: Coordinated turning is the starting observation.

questions.stimulus: Mosquitoes find hosts using carbon dioxide, body heat and skin chemicals. Traps that release only carbon dioxide catch some mosquitoes but far fewer than traps baited with skin odour as well. When researchers removed carbon dioxide entirely, the traps caught almost nothing, even with skin odour present. Carbon dioxide appears to be necessary, though not sufficient on its own.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the structure of the text?

choices.text: It argues that skin odour alone is sufficient to attract mosquitoes.
It lists cues, then reports comparisons that establish the role of one cue.
It describes a single cue and ignores the others.
It explains how to build a trap without evaluating any cue.

questions.explanation: The candidates are introduced together, and the trap comparisons isolate carbon dioxide as necessary but not sufficient.

distractor_rationales.C: All three cues are introduced.
distractor_rationales.A: Traps with skin odour but no carbon dioxide caught almost nothing.
distractor_rationales.D: The comparisons evaluate the cues.

questions.stimulus: Steel in seawater corrodes faster than steel in fresh water because chloride ions break down the protective oxide layer. Cathodic protection counteracts this by supplying electrons from a sacrificial metal that corrodes in place of the steel. The sacrificial block is replaced periodically; the structure it protects is not.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the structure of the text?

choices.text: It describes a method of protection without explaining why corrosion happens.
It compares two metals and argues that both corrode at the same rate.
It describes the manufacture of steel from iron ore.
It explains a cause of corrosion and then describes a method that prevents it.

questions.explanation: The chloride attack is the mechanism, and the sacrificial anode is the countermeasure that takes the corrosion instead.

distractor_rationales.B: The text says steel corrodes faster in seawater.
distractor_rationales.A: The chloride mechanism is explained first.
distractor_rationales.C: Manufacturing is not discussed.

questions.stimulus: Folding a flat sheet into a rigid structure usually requires glue or fasteners. A pattern of folds can instead lock the sheet into a stiff three-dimensional shape by creating ridges that resist bending. Engineers have used such patterns for packaging that ships flat and for panels that deploy in space. The fold pattern replaces the fastener.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.text: To describe the history of paper folding as an art form
To explain how folding can provide rigidity without added fasteners
To argue that flat sheets cannot be made rigid by any means
To compare the cost of packaging with the cost of spacecraft panels

questions.explanation: The passage's point is that ridges from folds resist bending, so the fold pattern itself does the work of glue or fasteners.

distractor_rationales.D: No costs are compared.
distractor_rationales.A: Origami as art is not discussed.
distractor_rationales.C: The text shows one way to make a sheet rigid.

questions.stimulus: Pigments in cave paintings include iron oxides, charcoal and minerals ground from local rock. Analysis of a paint layer can identify its ingredients, and comparison with nearby deposits can suggest where each came from. Some pigments were carried tens of kilometres, which implies that the painters chose materials for color or durability rather than convenience alone.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the structure of the text?

choices.text: It argues that cave painters used only materials found at the site.
It lists pigments without saying what they reveal.
It describes a painting technique and recommends it to modern artists.
It describes an analysis and then draws an inference from its results.

questions.explanation: The ingredient analysis is the method, and the long-distance sourcing is the inference about why materials were chosen.

distractor_rationales.C: No recommendation is made.
distractor_rationales.B: The pigments are linked to sourcing and choice.
distractor_rationales.A: The text says some pigments were carried long distances.

questions.stimulus: A single seismic station can record an earthquake but cannot locate it precisely. Three stations that record the same event allow location, because the arrival times differ by distance and the differences define a point. Networks therefore place stations in arrays rather than at isolated sites. The network, not the instrument, does the locating.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the structure of the text?

choices.text: It states a limitation, explains how combining stations overcomes it, and draws a design conclusion.
It describes an instrument and then lists its components.
It argues that isolated stations are more useful than networks.
It compares two types of earthquake and explains their origins.

questions.explanation: The single-station limit, the three-station solution, and the resulting preference for arrays form the passage's logic.

distractor_rationales.D: Earthquake types are not compared.
distractor_rationales.B: Components are not listed.
distractor_rationales.C: The text concludes the opposite.

questions.stimulus: Lichen grows so slowly that its hold on a gravestone can serve as a clock. Researchers measure the largest thallus on a stone and divide its radius by a growth rate calibrated to the local climate. On churchyard monuments of known age, the method usually lands within a few years. It fails on porous limestone and in polluted air, where growth stalls unpredictably.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Porous limestone offers the most reliable setting for lichen dating.
Churchyard monuments are usually older than their inscriptions claim.
Lichen grows quickly enough to record the exact year a stone was carved.
Lichen size can estimate the age of a gravestone, but only under favorable conditions.

questions.explanation: The passage explains the dating method, notes its apparent accuracy on dated monuments, and then names two conditions that break it.

distractor_rationales.C: The text calls lichen a slow grower, not a fast one.
distractor_rationales.B: No claim is made about inscriptions being wrong.
distractor_rationales.A: Limestone is named as one of the surfaces where the method fails.

questions.stimulus: Before the nineteenth century, most European paper was made from linen rags. Cotton and linen fibres are long and interlock into a sheet that resists acid. When cheap wood pulp replaced rags, paper became far more plentiful, but the pulp carried lignin and residual acids that slowly break fibre bonds. Libraries now spend large sums on chemical treatment for volumes printed after 1850.
questions.prompt: Which choice best explains why books printed after 1850 often need conservation?

choices.text: Later books were manufactured on thinner paper to cut transport weight.
Libraries stored the newer volumes in damper rooms than the older ones.
Post-1850 ink corrodes the binding thread faster than earlier ink.
Wood pulp introduced acids and lignin that weaken the paper over time.

questions.explanation: The passage contrasts acid-resistant rag paper with acidic, lignin-bearing wood pulp and ties the conservation expense to that shift.

distractor_rationales.C: Ink is not mentioned; the change is in the paper itself.
distractor_rationales.A: Thickness is not offered as a cause.
distractor_rationales.B: Storage conditions are never compared in the text.

questions.stimulus: A peat bog is a waterlogged archive. Because standing water excludes oxygen and slows decay, plant material accumulates for thousands of years. Each layer records the pollen that fell that season, so a core from a bog reads like a calendar of regional vegetation. Draining a bog for fuel or farmland reverses the guarantee: oxygen enters, decay resumes, and the archive is lost.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Peat burns well because it holds very little water.
Bog cores record animal populations more reliably than plants.
Draining a bog speeds up the formation of new peat layers.
Bogs preserve layered evidence of past vegetation only while they remain wet.

questions.explanation: The passage explains how waterlogged conditions stop decay and create a pollen record, then warns that drainage destroys it.

distractor_rationales.A: The text stresses that bogs are waterlogged, not water-poor.
distractor_rationales.B: Pollen is the recorded evidence, not animals.
distractor_rationales.C: Draining is described as ending preservation, not aiding it.

questions.stimulus: Bats that hunt near foliage use long, low-frequency calls that travel well but resolve detail poorly. Bats hunting in cluttered woods switch to brief, high-frequency calls that fade quickly yet return sharp echoes from nearby shapes. When researchers recorded a single species hunting in both habitats, the calls matched the setting rather than the animal: individuals changed call design as they crossed from open field to canopy.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: High-frequency calls travel farther than low-frequency calls.
Each bat species uses one fixed call design from birth.
Open-field hunting demands sharper detail than hunting inside woods.
Bats adjust their calls to the habitat they are hunting in at that moment.

questions.explanation: The passage gives the trade-off between call designs, then reports that one species changed its design as it moved between habitats.

distractor_rationales.B: The recorded individuals changed calls within one species.
distractor_rationales.A: The text says high-frequency calls fade quickly, so they travel less far.
distractor_rationales.C: It is the cluttered woods that require resolution of nearby shapes.

questions.stimulus: Bamboo scaffolding still rises around skyscrapers in some cities. The traditional material is cheap, light enough to be carried by hand, and quickly cut to length. Critics point to fire risk and to the absence of formal design codes. Practitioners answer that the lashings are the structure: a properly tied joint spreads load across several culms, so the frame gives slightly instead of snapping in typhoon winds.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Bamboo scaffolding has replaced steel on most high-rise construction sites.
Fire risk has made bamboo scaffolding unacceptable in every city.
Bamboo scaffolding offers genuine structural advantages, though it also carries risks.
Lashings are decorative and play no part in supporting the frame.

questions.explanation: The passage balances practical advantages against fire and code concerns, then explains how tied joints distribute load.

distractor_rationales.A: The text says "some cities," not most sites.
distractor_rationales.B: Risk is acknowledged but not described as a universal ban.
distractor_rationales.D: The passage calls the lashings the structure itself.

questions.stimulus: Seed banks cannot simply freeze every seed and forget it. Some species die if dried to the standard moisture level; others survive only if cooled slowly. Germination tests therefore run on samples withdrawn at fixed intervals, and a fraction of each collection is regrown so fresh seed replaces ageing stock. A bank's value lies less in its freezer than in this repeated cycle of testing and renewal.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Seed banks regrow samples only when a species becomes extinct in the wild.
Germination tests are performed once, when a collection first arrives.
Keeping seeds viable requires ongoing testing and regeneration, not storage alone.
Freezing at a single standard moisture level works for all species.

questions.explanation: The passage lists species-specific handling, describes periodic testing and regrowth, and concludes that this cycle is the bank's real value.

distractor_rationales.D: The text names species that die at the standard level.
distractor_rationales.A: Regrowth is routine renewal, not a response to extinction.
distractor_rationales.B: Tests run at fixed intervals throughout storage.

questions.stimulus: On some glaciers, small balls of moss roll slowly downhill as the ice moves beneath them. The balls stay green on the outside and die at the base, where they touch the ice. Because each ball turns only as fast as the surface it rides, its motion is set by the glacier rather than by the wind. Researchers have used them as passive markers of ice flow.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Glacier moss balls are blown downhill by strong katabatic winds.
Researchers move the balls deliberately to chart ice movement.
Glacier moss balls move with the ice and can therefore serve as markers of its flow.
The moss stays alive throughout the ball, including where it meets the ice.

questions.explanation: The passage describes the balls, explains that ice movement drives them, and states that researchers use them as passive flow markers.

distractor_rationales.A: The text says motion is set by the glacier, not by wind.
distractor_rationales.D: The base dies where it touches the ice.
distractor_rationales.B: They are passive markers, not tools the researchers reposition.

questions.stimulus: Tide pools high on a rocky shore heat up faster than pools near the waterline. During low tide on a sunny day, a shallow upper pool can climb several degrees above the surrounding ocean. Species that cannot tolerate the swing retreat downward, leaving the upper pools to a few heat-tolerant specialists. On cool, foggy coasts the same pools stay far closer to ocean temperature.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: A pool's height on the shore shapes how extreme its temperature becomes and which species survive there.
Foggy coasts produce the widest temperature swings in tide pools.
Upper tide pools are always cooler than pools near the waterline.
All tide-pool species tolerate the same range of temperatures.

questions.explanation: The passage links pool height to temperature extremes, notes that sensitive species move down, and contrasts sunny with foggy coasts.

distractor_rationales.C: The text says upper pools heat faster and climb higher.
distractor_rationales.D: Species differ in tolerance, which is why some retreat.
distractor_rationales.B: Foggy coasts keep pools closer to ocean temperature.

questions.stimulus: The painted clay figures buried near Xi'an retained traces of pigment because the burial chamber stayed dark, dry and chemically stable. Once excavated, the surface met air and light for the first time in two thousand years. Conservators now record color within minutes of exposure, and some figures are reburied rather than displayed, because the safest environment for the paint is the one it left.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: The figures were originally painted with pigments that resist light.
Reburial damages the paint more than museum display does.
Conservators display every figure as soon as it is excavated.
The pigment survives best in the buried conditions that exposure destroys.

questions.explanation: The passage credits the stable burial chamber, describes the threat posed by air and light, and explains choices made to protect the paint.

distractor_rationales.A: The text says exposure damages the paint; it never calls it light-resistant.
distractor_rationales.C: Some figures are reburied instead of displayed.
distractor_rationales.B: Reburial is described as the safer option.

questions.stimulus: A subway diagram is not a map. To make routes readable, designers straighten lines, space stations evenly and enlarge the city center. The result distorts distance so badly that a two-stop ride downtown may be shorter on the ground than a one-stop ride in the suburbs. Riders accept the distortion because the diagram answers the question they actually ask: which line to take, not how far they will travel.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Subway diagrams are drawn to preserve true geographic distance.
Outer stations are always spaced more widely than central ones.
Subway diagrams deliberately distort distance in order to make routes easier to follow.
Riders reject diagrams that fail to show exact travel distances.

questions.explanation: The passage describes the distortions, gives an example of their effect, and explains why riders tolerate them.

distractor_rationales.A: The text says designers straighten lines and space stations evenly.
distractor_rationales.D: The passage says riders accept the distortion.
distractor_rationales.B: Central stations are enlarged and spread out, not the reverse.

questions.stimulus: A sourdough starter is a stable community of wild yeasts and lactic-acid bacteria. Feed it flour and water on a regular schedule and the same species tend to dominate for years, even if the kitchen is not sterile. Change the feeding rhythm or the flour, however, and the balance shifts. Bakers describe the result as a change in character: sharper, slower to rise, or suddenly vigorous.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Sterile kitchens are required to keep a starter free of unwanted microbes.
A starter's species composition never changes once it is established.
Switching flour has no measurable effect on how a starter behaves.
A starter's microbial balance stays stable under routine feeding but responds to changes in it.

questions.explanation: The passage presents the starter as a stable community, then describes how feeding rhythm and flour change its behavior.

distractor_rationales.A: The text says the community persists even in an unsterile kitchen.
distractor_rationales.B: The passage says the balance shifts when conditions change.
distractor_rationales.C: Flour is named as one of the changes that alters the balance.

questions.stimulus: Ice cores preserve dust in annual layers. A band rich in mineral dust usually marks a year when winds carried more material from exposed ground, often during a dry period. Because the layers are ordered and countable, a core gives both a sequence of events and a rough timescale. The dust itself does not measure temperature; it records atmospheric transport, which researchers interpret alongside other signals.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Dust layers in ice cores are a direct measurement of past temperature.
Ice-core layers cannot be counted, so they provide no timescale.
Mineral dust in ice cores comes mainly from volcanic eruptions.
Dust layers in ice cores record atmospheric transport and give a dated sequence, not a direct temperature reading.

questions.explanation: The passage explains what a dust band represents, notes the countable layering, and limits the interpretation to atmospheric transport.

distractor_rationales.A: The text explicitly denies that dust measures temperature.
distractor_rationales.B: It says the layers are countable and give a rough timescale.
distractor_rationales.C: The dust is described as wind-blown from exposed ground.

questions.stimulus: When a whale carcass sinks, it supports a succession of communities for decades. Scavengers strip soft tissue within months. Bone-eating worms and mussels then colonise the skeleton, using fats locked inside the bone. Only after those reserves are exhausted do sulphide-loving microbes take over the remaining mineral structure. The same carcass passes through several distinct ecosystems without moving.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Bone-eating species arrive before soft tissue scavengers.
A single sunken carcass supports a long sequence of different communities as its resources are used up.
Whale carcasses are consumed entirely within a few months of sinking.
The communities at a carcass all depend on the same food source.

questions.explanation: The passage orders the stages of a whale fall and shows that each community exploits a different remaining resource.

distractor_rationales.C: The text says the process lasts for decades.
distractor_rationales.A: Scavengers strip soft tissue first, then bone specialists arrive.
distractor_rationales.D: Each stage uses a different resource, from tissue to bone fat to minerals.

questions.stimulus: Before radio, fire lookouts located fires by triangulation. Two towers sighted the same smoke plume and reported the bearing from each. Drawn on a map, the two bearings crossed at a single point. Accuracy depended on clear sightlines and on towers being far enough apart that the lines met at a wide angle; towers nearly in line produced a crossing so shallow that a small error moved the reported fire by miles.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Fire lookouts relied on radio to report bearings before triangulation.
Towers placed close together produced the most accurate crossings.
A single lookout could locate a fire without help from another tower.
Triangulation worked well only when the sighting towers were positioned to produce a wide crossing angle.

questions.explanation: The passage describes the two-bearing method and explains why wide angles made the crossing reliable while shallow ones amplified error.

distractor_rationales.C: The method requires two bearings from two towers.
distractor_rationales.A: The text places triangulation before radio.
distractor_rationales.B: Close or nearly aligned towers produced shallow, inaccurate crossings.

questions.stimulus: Oyster reefs once formed low walls along many estuaries. The shells break incoming waves before the water reaches the shore, and the spaces between them shelter juvenile fish. When reefs were dredged away for lime and road fill, shorelines began to erode faster. Restoration projects now lay shell bags in shallow water, where new larvae settle on old shell and rebuild the structure over several seasons.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Dredging reefs improved shoreline stability in most estuaries.
Oyster reefs increase wave energy reaching the shore.
Oyster reefs protect shorelines and can be rebuilt by giving larvae a shell base to settle on.
Restored reefs form within a single season without intervention.

questions.explanation: The passage describes the protective role of reefs, the consequence of removing them, and the shell-bag method of restoration.

distractor_rationales.B: The text says reefs break waves before they reach shore.
distractor_rationales.D: Rebuilding takes several seasons.
distractor_rationales.A: Dredging is linked to faster erosion.

questions.stimulus: Japanese joinery connects beams without nails or glue. A dovetail or mortise-and-tenon joint relies on shaped surfaces that lock together under load, and a well-cut joint can be dismantled and reassembled without losing grip. The technique demands precise handwork, since a gap of a millimetre defeats the interlock. Modern timber frames sometimes combine such joints with concealed steel, using the metal where the wood alone would creep.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Wooden joints can carry structural loads through precise shaping, though modern practice sometimes adds hidden reinforcement.
Machine-cut joints are more precise than hand-cut ones and have replaced them.
Japanese joinery depends on glue to hold its shaped surfaces together.
Steel reinforcement makes traditional joints impossible to dismantle.

questions.explanation: The passage explains how interlocking shapes carry load, stresses the need for precision, and notes where modern builders add concealed steel.

distractor_rationales.C: The text says the joints use no nails or glue.
distractor_rationales.B: Precision is attributed to handwork, not machines.
distractor_rationales.D: The passage does not say reinforced frames cannot be dismantled.

questions.stimulus: Tea leaves begin to oxidise as soon as they are rolled. To make green tea, growers heat the leaves quickly to stop the reaction; to make black tea, they let it run. The same bush can therefore produce either style. What changes is not the plant but the moment at which the process is halted, which is why a single garden may sell several very different teas from one harvest.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Black tea is made by halting oxidation immediately after rolling.
A single garden can produce only one style of tea per harvest.
The style of tea depends on when oxidation is stopped, not on a different plant.
Green tea and black tea come from different species of bush.

questions.explanation: The passage contrasts the two processes and concludes that timing, not the plant, determines the style.

distractor_rationales.D: The text says the same bush can produce either style.
distractor_rationales.A: Black tea lets oxidation continue.
distractor_rationales.B: One harvest can yield several styles.

questions.stimulus: Most microplastic fibres in coastal water come from clothing. Washing releases them because fabric rubs against itself in the drum, breaking weak filaments. Filters fitted to washing machines catch a share of the fibres, but the smallest fragments pass through. Researchers therefore compare fibre loads downstream of treatment plants with those from households, trying to separate what a plant removes from what it simply delays.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Machine filters capture every fibre released during a wash.
Treatment plants prevent all microplastic fibres from reaching the sea.
Microplastic fibres in coastal water originate mainly from fishing gear.
Washing clothes releases microplastic fibres that treatment plants only partly remove.

questions.explanation: The passage names washing as the main source, explains the release mechanism, and notes that filters and plants capture only part of the load.

distractor_rationales.C: The text identifies clothing as the main source.
distractor_rationales.A: The smallest fragments pass through filters.
distractor_rationales.B: The plants capture a share, not everything.

questions.stimulus: In dry regions, a sand dam is built across a seasonal riverbed. During the rains, sand washes down and lodges behind the wall, and water fills the pores between the grains. Because the sand shields the water from sun and evaporation, the stored supply can outlast an open reservoir of similar volume. Wells sunk into the sand then draw water through the dry season.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Sand dams are open reservoirs that lose water quickly to evaporation.
Sand dams store water in the pores of trapped sand, which limits evaporation and keeps supply available through dry months.
The wall of a sand dam blocks sand while allowing water to pass downstream.
Wells dug into sand dams yield water only during the rainy season.

questions.explanation: The passage describes how sand collects behind the wall, how water is held between grains, and why that limits evaporation.

distractor_rationales.A: The text says the sand shields the water, unlike an open reservoir.
distractor_rationales.C: The wall traps the sand, and water is held among the grains.
distractor_rationales.D: Wells draw on the stored water through the dry season.

questions.stimulus: Many birds moult their flight feathers on a schedule that avoids the demands of migration and breeding. Waterfowl often drop all primaries at once and cannot fly for several weeks, so they gather on open water where predators are easier to see. Smaller songbirds replace feathers gradually, keeping enough lift to fly throughout. Both strategies are ways of managing the same trade-off between repair and mobility.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Moult strategies differ because birds balance feather replacement against the need to stay mobile.
All birds replace their flight feathers at exactly the same time of year.
Songbirds moult only when they have finished migrating for the year.
Waterfowl keep flying normally while they replace every primary feather.

questions.explanation: The passage contrasts simultaneous and gradual moult and explains that both manage the trade-off between repair and staying airborne.

distractor_rationales.B: The passage describes two different schedules.
distractor_rationales.D: Waterfowl cannot fly for weeks after dropping all primaries.
distractor_rationales.C: The text does not tie songbird moult to migration completion.

questions.stimulus: Lunar soil contains no organic binder, so engineers have tested sintering it with microwaves into solid bricks. The process melts grains at contact points, fusing them without additives. A furnace would have to carry its own power and mass to the Moon, which makes the energy budget the central design constraint. Tests on simulated regolith show that bricks strong enough for a landing pad are possible, but only at temperatures that demand substantial equipment.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Sintering lunar soil can make strong bricks, but the energy and equipment required are the main obstacles.
Lunar soil already contains a natural binder that holds bricks together.
Engineers have built landing pads on the Moon from sintered regolith.
Microwave sintering requires additives shipped from Earth.

questions.explanation: The passage explains the sintering method, identifies energy as the constraint, and limits the result to laboratory tests.

distractor_rationales.B: The text says the soil has no organic binder.
distractor_rationales.C: The tests are on simulated regolith on Earth.
distractor_rationales.D: The process fuses grains without additives.

questions.stimulus: A hand-bound book is held together by thread sewn through the folds of its sections. The sewing must be tight enough to keep the pages aligned but loose enough that the spine can open without cracking the paper. Binders therefore choose thread thickness and stitch spacing for the paper in front of them. A method that works for heavy drawing paper will tear thin text paper at the fold.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Tight sewing is always better because it prevents pages from shifting.
Thread thickness has no effect on whether a spine can open.
Binding choices must be matched to the paper, because a stitch that suits one paper damages another.
Hand binding uses glue instead of thread to hold sections together.

questions.explanation: The passage explains the tension in sewing, then states that thread and spacing are selected per paper, with a concrete failure example.

distractor_rationales.D: The text describes thread sewn through folds.
distractor_rationales.A: The passage warns that too tight a stitch cracks the paper.
distractor_rationales.B: Thread thickness is named as a choice binders make.

questions.stimulus: Beavers change the hydrology of a valley long before anyone measures it. A dam raises the water table, slows spring runoff and spreads water across the floodplain. Downstream, the peak of a flood arrives later and lower. Removing beavers reverses the effect quickly, which is why some water managers now treat them as inexpensive infrastructure rather than as nuisance rodents.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Water managers universally regard beavers as pests to be removed.
Beaver activity has no measurable effect on the water table.
Beaver dams alter water storage and timing in ways that can be useful to water managers.
Beaver dams raise flood peaks downstream.

questions.explanation: The passage describes the hydrological effects and notes that managers increasingly value them.

distractor_rationales.D: The text says the downstream peak arrives later and lower.
distractor_rationales.B: The dam is said to raise the water table.
distractor_rationales.A: The passage describes a shift toward treating them as infrastructure.

questions.stimulus: Soil microbes respire carbon the way animals do, releasing it as carbon dioxide. Whether a soil stores or loses carbon depends on how much of that respiration is offset by plant inputs and by organic matter sticking to mineral surfaces. Warming speeds microbial activity, but it can also dry the soil and reduce plant growth. The net effect therefore varies by site, which is why estimates from one grassland do not transfer to another.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Whether warming makes a soil a carbon source or sink depends on local conditions.
Soil microbes store carbon directly in their cells without respiring.
Warming always causes soil to release more carbon than it stores.
Results from one grassland reliably predict another's carbon balance.

questions.explanation: The passage sets respiration against plant inputs and mineral binding, then concludes that the outcome is site-specific.

distractor_rationales.C: The text says the net effect varies.
distractor_rationales.B: Microbes are described as respiring carbon dioxide.
