Clippers carried bulk cargo more cheaply after the canal opened.
The Suez Canal made the clippers' route shorter than the steamships'.

questions.explanation: The canal favored steam, eroding the clipper's niche.

distractor_rationales.D: Steamships took the shorter route the clippers could not use.
distractor_rationales.C: Clippers carried light, high-value cargo.
distractor_rationales.A: The passage says the narrow hull reduced capacity.

questions.stimulus: A bell foundry casts a bell slightly larger than its final size because tuning removes metal. The founder also adjusts the profile so that the bell's partial tones form the intended chord. Changing the profile after casting is nearly impossible, so the shape must be right before the metal cools.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Tuning adds metal to raise the pitch.
The partial tones are unrelated to the bell's shape.
A bell's profile can be reshaped easily after casting.
Most of a bell's tonal character is fixed at casting, with tuning only refining it.

questions.explanation: Since profile cannot be changed later, the cast shape carries the tonal design.

distractor_rationales.C: The passage says reshaping after casting is nearly impossible.
distractor_rationales.A: Tuning removes metal.
distractor_rationales.B: The profile is adjusted to shape the partials.

questions.stimulus: An oyster reef filters water as its inhabitants feed. A dense reef can clear suspended particles from a large volume in a day. When reefs were removed, water clarity fell and sunlight reached less deeply. Seagrasses, which need light, declined in the same estuaries.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Water clarity improved after reefs were removed.
Oyster reefs increase suspended particles in the water.
Losing oyster reefs can reduce water clarity enough to harm seagrass.
Seagrasses grow better in turbid water.

questions.explanation: Filtration loss, lower clarity and seagrass decline form the causal chain.

distractor_rationales.B: The reef filters particles out.
distractor_rationales.D: Seagrass needs light, which turbidity blocks.
distractor_rationales.A: The passage says clarity fell.

questions.stimulus: A mudbrick wall shrinks as it dries. If the outer surface dries faster than the core, the difference in shrinkage pulls the surface apart. Builders therefore mix straw into the clay, which slows drying and gives the shrinking mass something to hold onto. The cracks that appear in unstrawed brick begin at the surface.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Mudbrick does not change size as it dries.
Straw reduces cracking by evening out the drying of a mudbrick.
Straw speeds drying and increases surface shrinkage.
Cracks in unstrawed brick start at the core.

questions.explanation: Straw moderates the moisture gradient that causes surface cracking.

distractor_rationales.C: The passage says straw slows drying.
distractor_rationales.A: The wall shrinks as it dries.
distractor_rationales.D: The text says cracks begin at the surface.

questions.stimulus: Goats browse young trees before they can grow above reach. On islands where goats were removed, tree lines moved upslope within decades. On islands where goats remained, the same species stayed low and sparse. The difference between the islands tracks the presence of goats rather than climate.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Goats help young trees grow above browsing height.
Removing goats prevented trees from spreading.
Grazing animals can hold a tree line in place.
Tree lines are determined entirely by temperature.

questions.explanation: The island comparison isolates grazing as the cause.

distractor_rationales.D: The paired islands share climate but differ in goats.
distractor_rationales.B: Tree lines moved upslope after removal.
distractor_rationales.A: Goats browse young trees before they escape reach.

questions.stimulus: Lichens absorb water and nutrients directly through their surfaces, which also means they absorb pollutants. A lichen transplanted from a clean site to a city center accumulates metals within months. Species differ in tolerance, so a survey of which lichens survive can map pollution without instruments.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Lichens filter out pollutants and remain unaffected.
Lichen communities can act as biological pollution monitors.
All lichen species respond to pollution in the same way.

questions.explanation: Absorption plus species-specific tolerance supports biomonitoring.

distractor_rationales.A: The passage says they absorb pollutants.
distractor_rationales.C: Tolerance differs by species.
distractor_rationales.D: The transplant accumulated metals within months.

questions.stimulus: Dredging records show how often a harbour was cleared. Sediment cores show layers of coarse material where dredging mixed the bed. Where the two records agree, historians can date a period of increased shipping. Where they disagree, one source is probably incomplete.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Disagreement proves both records are correct.
Agreement between independent records strengthens a claim about harbour use.
Dredging records and sediment cores always agree.
Coarse sediment indicates that no dredging occurred.

questions.explanation: Cross-checking two independent records is what supports the dating.

distractor_rationales.C: The passage describes cases where they disagree.
distractor_rationales.D: Mixed beds leave coarse layers.
distractor_rationales.A: Disagreement is explained as incompleteness in one source.

questions.stimulus: In permafrost, ice wedges form when meltwater enters cracks and refreezes. Repeated widening pushes the surrounding ground upward and outward, creating patterned polygons at the surface. Where the climate warms, wedges melt and the polygons subside. The pattern is therefore a visible record of ground temperature.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: The patterns are unrelated to temperature.
Melting ice wedges raises the ground surface.
Changing polygon patterns can signal thawing permafrost.
Polygons form only where the ground never freezes.

questions.explanation: The surface pattern tracks the state of the ice wedges.

distractor_rationales.D: Freezing meltwater is the mechanism.
distractor_rationales.B: Melting causes subsidence.
distractor_rationales.A: The passage links the pattern to ground temperature.

questions.stimulus: A fresco is painted on wet lime plaster. As the plaster sets, the pigment becomes part of the wall, which is why the color lasts. The painter must work quickly, because once the plaster dries the surface will not accept pigment in the same way. Frescoes were therefore planned in sections sized to one day's work.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: A painter could return to the same section weeks later.
The technique's durability depends on painting before the plaster sets.
Fresco pigment sits on top of dry plaster.
The sections were sized to the painter's arm length only.

questions.explanation: The wet-plaster window explains both durability and the daily section plan.

distractor_rationales.C: The pigment becomes part of the wall as it sets.
distractor_rationales.A: Dry plaster will not accept pigment the same way.
distractor_rationales.D: Sections matched a day's work, not arm length.

questions.stimulus: A bridge cable is protected from rust by a galvanised coating that corrodes before the steel beneath. The coating is sacrificial: it gives up metal so the cable does not. Once the coating is consumed, the steel begins to rust, so inspectors measure coating thickness rather than waiting for visible damage.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Inspectors should ignore the coating and wait for rust.
Measuring the protective layer gives earlier warning than looking for rust.
Galvanising makes steel immune to corrosion.
The coating outlasts the steel it protects.

questions.explanation: Coating thickness is an early indicator of remaining protection.

distractor_rationales.C: The coating corrodes so the steel does not.
distractor_rationales.A: By the time rust shows, the coating is gone.
distractor_rationales.D: Once consumed, the steel begins to rust.

questions.stimulus: A fish's otolith grows in annual rings, much like a tree. The rings record the temperature and chemistry of the water the fish inhabited, and a single otolith carries the whole life history of one animal. Researchers can therefore place a fish in particular waters at particular ages, even after it has been caught far away.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: An otolith changes after the fish dies, erasing its history.
Otoliths preserve a dated record of the environments a fish moved through.
Otolith rings record only the fish's age, not its environment.

questions.explanation: Annual layers with environmental chemistry allow life-history reconstruction.

distractor_rationales.D: The rings record water chemistry as well as age.
distractor_rationales.A: The record survives in the recovered ear stone.
distractor_rationales.C: The passage describes annual rings.

questions.stimulus: In stony deserts, stones sometimes sit on pedestals of fine soil. Wind removes the loose material around a stone but cannot lift the stone itself, so the ground beneath it erodes more slowly. Over time the stone appears to rise. The pedestal is therefore a record of wind erosion, not of the stone being pushed upward.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: The stone is gradually lifted by rising air currents.
Pedestals form only where the ground is fully protected from wind.
The surrounding ground has been lowered, leaving the stone elevated.
Wind deposits soil beneath the stone.

questions.explanation: Differential deflation lowers the surrounding plain.

distractor_rationales.A: Deflation removes material around the stone.
distractor_rationales.D: The pedestal remains because erosion is slower beneath the stone.
distractor_rationales.B: Wind erosion is the mechanism, not protection.

questions.stimulus: Many mushrooms fruit after rain, but rain alone is not enough. The mycelium must already have stored enough nutrients, and the air must cool enough to trigger development. A dry summer followed by a single storm often produces no flush, while a wet autumn with mild nights produces a large one.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: A single storm is sufficient to produce a mushroom flush.
Mycelium stores no nutrients before fruiting.
Mushrooms fruit best in dry, warm conditions.
Fruiting depends on accumulated reserves and temperature as well as moisture.

questions.explanation: The passage names three conditions, not one.

distractor_rationales.A: The passage says rain alone is not enough.
distractor_rationales.C: Cooling nights and wet weather favor fruiting.
distractor_rationales.B: Reserves are described as necessary.

questions.stimulus: People often assume that a desert is empty of life because it looks bare. A closer look at a single square meter of sand can reveal seeds, dormant eggs and buried insects waiting for rain. Within days of a storm, the same ground may be covered with seedlings and insects that were invisible before.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It compares two deserts and concludes that they are identical.
It states a common assumption and then presents evidence that contradicts it.
It lists several causes and ranks them by importance.
It describes a process step by step from beginning to end.

questions.explanation: The passage opens with an assumption, then offers hidden life as the correction.

distractor_rationales.C: There is no ranking of causes.
distractor_rationales.D: No sequential process is described.
distractor_rationales.A: Only one setting is discussed.

questions.stimulus: A hand loom and a power loom produce the same cloth, but they organize work differently. On a hand loom the weaver controls pace and pattern at every pass. A power loom fixes the pace and moves pattern control into the punch card or the computer. The change is less about speed than about where decisions sit.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To explain how mechanisation shifted control over pattern and pace away from the weaver.
To describe the technical steps of warping a loom.
To show that power looms produce no patterned cloth.
To argue that hand-woven cloth is of better quality.

questions.explanation: The passage contrasts two looms and locates the real change in decision-making.

distractor_rationales.D: Quality is not compared.
distractor_rationales.B: Warping is never mentioned.
distractor_rationales.C: Pattern control is relocated, not eliminated.

questions.stimulus: Early maps of the ocean floor were assembled from lead lines dropped over the side. Each sounding gave one depth at one point. A century later, sonar surveyed whole swaths in a single pass. The difference is not merely accuracy: it is the shift from a scatter of points to a continuous surface.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It argues that early maps were more accurate than sonar maps.
It contrasts two surveying methods and explains what the change made possible.
It narrates a single voyage in chronological order.
It lists the materials used to build sounding lines.

questions.explanation: The passage juxtaposes lead-line and sonar surveys and names the conceptual gain.

distractor_rationales.C: No voyage is described.
distractor_rationales.D: Materials are not listed.
distractor_rationales.A: Sonar is presented as the advance.

questions.stimulus: A paper conservator faced with a brittle volume has two options. Washing removes acid but risks the ink. Deacidification spray neutralises acid with less moisture but penetrates unevenly. The choice depends on the ink, the paper and how much time the collection can spare.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It explains why brittle paper cannot be treated at all.
It presents two options, notes the risk of each, and says the choice is conditional.
It describes the history of paper manufacture in order.
It recommends one treatment as correct in every case.

questions.explanation: Two treatments, their risks, and conditional advice structure the passage.

distractor_rationales.D: The passage says the choice is conditional.
distractor_rationales.C: No manufacturing history is given.
distractor_rationales.A: Treatments are offered, not ruled out.

questions.stimulus: Bamboo is often called a grass, and the label matters. It grows from an underground rhizome, sends up hollow stems, and dies back after flowering. Each of these traits is shared with grasses and not with the trees it resembles. The resemblance to wood is a matter of size, not of family.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To describe how bamboo is harvested and dried.
To explain why bamboo's botanical traits place it with grasses rather than trees.
To compare the strength of bamboo and steel.
To argue that bamboo should be classified as a hardwood.

questions.explanation: Shared grass traits are the evidence behind the classification.

distractor_rationales.D: The passage separates bamboo from trees.
distractor_rationales.A: Harvesting is not discussed.
distractor_rationales.C: No strength comparison appears.

questions.stimulus: A new bridge design was tested in a wind tunnel at increasing speeds. At low speeds the deck behaved as predicted. At a critical speed the deck began to twist, and the twisting grew instead of settling. The test was stopped, and the section was reshaped before the next run.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It compares two bridge designs and declares one superior.
It explains the theory of wind loading without describing a test.
It lists several failures from different laboratories.
It narrates a test in sequence and ends with the response to a failure.

questions.explanation: The passage follows the test from low speed to failure to redesign.

distractor_rationales.A: Only one design is tested.
distractor_rationales.B: A concrete test is described.
distractor_rationales.C: There is a single test sequence.

questions.stimulus: Salt marshes absorb wave energy, store carbon and shelter young fish. They also migrate inland as sea level rises, but only if the land behind them is open. Where a seawall blocks that retreat, the marsh is squeezed against a hard edge and drowns. Protection therefore depends on what lies behind the marsh.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It describes the formation of salt marshes from bare mud.
It argues that seawalls are the best way to protect marshes.
It lists benefits, introduces a condition for survival, and draws a conclusion about that condition.
It compares marshes in two countries and finds no difference.

questions.explanation: Benefits, a migration condition, and the blocking seawall build to the conclusion.

distractor_rationales.A: Formation from mud is not described.
distractor_rationales.B: Seawalls are the obstacle in the example.
distractor_rationales.D: No country comparison appears.

questions.stimulus: The claim that goldfish have three-second memories is repeated so often that it has become a fact in popular telling. Experiments with trained fish show them returning to a feeding site weeks later. The repetition of the claim, not the evidence, explains its persistence.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To confirm that goldfish memory lasts only seconds.
To challenge a widely repeated claim by pointing to contrary evidence.
To explain how to train a goldfish to feed on cue.
To describe the anatomy of the goldfish brain.

questions.explanation: The passage sets a popular claim against experimental evidence and explains its persistence.

distractor_rationales.C: Training is mentioned as evidence, not as instruction.
distractor_rationales.A: The passage contradicts the three-second claim.
distractor_rationales.D: Anatomy is never discussed.

questions.stimulus: A weaver preparing a warp winds hundreds of threads onto a beam, keeping each at even tension. If one thread is tighter, it pulls the cloth out of shape later. The preparation is slow and invisible in the finished fabric, which is why it is easy to skimp and expensive to get wrong.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To compare two kinds of loom in detail.
To describe the visible pattern of a finished cloth.
To explain why an invisible preparatory step matters to the final product.
To argue that warp preparation can safely be skipped.

questions.explanation: The passage connects an unseen preparation to a visible consequence.

distractor_rationales.B: The step's invisibility is the point.
distractor_rationales.D: Skimping is described as costly.
distractor_rationales.A: Looms are not compared here.

questions.stimulus: Some seeds remain dormant for decades even when conditions seem right. Scarification, whether by heat, abrasion or passage through an animal, can break that dormancy. The seed is not waiting passively; it is holding a lock that only particular events can open.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It describes an observation, illustrates it with examples, and closes with a comparison.
It argues that dormancy is simply a passive waiting period.
It lists the chemical steps of germination in order.
It presents a chronological history of seed science.

questions.explanation: Observation, examples, then the lock metaphor shape the passage.

distractor_rationales.D: No historical sequence is offered.
distractor_rationales.B: The final sentence rejects pure passivity.
distractor_rationales.C: Chemical steps are not given.

questions.stimulus: An acoustic engineer testing a lecture hall found that speech was clear in the front rows but muddled at the back. The ceiling reflected sound back to the front while the rear received echoes from a flat wall. Adding curved diffusers at the rear changed the pattern without adding amplification.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It argues that amplification is the only solution.
It compares two halls and finds both equally clear.
It describes a problem, identifies its cause, and reports a solution.
It lists materials used in hall construction.

questions.explanation: Problem, cause and remedy structure the paragraph.

distractor_rationales.B: Only one hall is discussed.
distractor_rationales.D: Materials are incidental.
distractor_rationales.A: The solution avoids amplification.

questions.stimulus: A river that once meandered across a floodplain was straightened for navigation. The shortened channel carried water away faster, which deepened the bed and lowered the water table beside it. Farmland that had relied on the high water table dried, and the river began to cut downward rather than spread sideways.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It traces a chain of consequences that followed a single alteration.
It argues that straightening a river has no downstream effects.
It describes the construction of a navigation lock.
It compares two rivers and ranks their water quality.

questions.explanation: The paragraph moves from straightening to deepening to a lowered water table and dried farmland.

distractor_rationales.D: One river is followed.
distractor_rationales.C: No lock construction is described.
distractor_rationales.B: Consequences are the subject of the passage.

questions.stimulus: A museum label once told visitors that a wooden mask was used in ceremonies. No record supported the claim. When the catalog was revised, the label was replaced with a note that the mask's use is unknown and that the wood dates to the twelfth century. The absence of evidence became part of the display.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To prove that the mask was used in ceremonies.
To show how acknowledging missing evidence can improve an exhibit.
To describe the carving techniques used on the mask.
To explain how wooden objects are dated by museums.

questions.explanation: The revision turns an unsupported claim into an honest label.

distractor_rationales.C: Carving is not described.
distractor_rationales.A: The passage says the ceremony claim lacked support.
distractor_rationales.D: Dating is mentioned but not explained.

questions.stimulus: Two methods exist for measuring a forest's carbon. One counts every tree in sample plots and estimates the rest. The other uses laser scanning from an aircraft to map canopy height. Plot counts are accurate but slow; scanning is fast but needs calibration against plots. Neither stands alone.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It argues that forest carbon cannot be measured.
It describes a single method in step-by-step detail.
It compares two methods, names the limits of each, and concludes that they depend on one another.
It recommends abandoning plot counts in favor of scanning.

questions.explanation: The contrast and the calibration requirement produce the joint conclusion.

distractor_rationales.D: Plot counts are needed for calibration.
distractor_rationales.B: Two methods are compared.
distractor_rationales.A: Measurement is described as possible.

questions.stimulus: A bell is rung once and the sound continues for many seconds. A listener hears a fundamental note plus weaker tones above it. The shape of the bell determines which of those tones are strong, and shifting one part of the profile can make a bell sound bright or dull without changing its fundamental pitch.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To describe the metal alloy used in bell casting.
To explain how a bell's shape shapes its tone beyond the fundamental note.
To argue that a bell produces only one tone.
To explain how bell ringers time their strokes.

questions.explanation: The passage links profile shape to the strength of upper tones.

distractor_rationales.A: Alloy is not mentioned.
distractor_rationales.C: The passage describes multiple tones.
distractor_rationales.D: Ringing technique is not discussed.

questions.stimulus: Coastal dunes form when wind carries sand inland until vegetation slows it. The plants trap grains, and the dune grows upward. A single storm can cut the dune back, but the roots usually survive. The dune is therefore built slowly and destroyed quickly, a pattern that shapes how coastlines are managed.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It explains a formation process, notes a countervailing force, and draws a management implication.
It argues that storms build dunes faster than vegetation does.
It lists the plant species found on dunes.
It tells the history of one particular coastline.

questions.explanation: Growth, storm damage and management follow one another.

distractor_rationales.D: No specific coastline is followed.
distractor_rationales.B: Storms cut dunes back.
distractor_rationales.C: Species are not listed.

questions.stimulus: Every year the same lake freezes later than it did a century ago. Records kept by a monastery note the first day of ice each winter. The series is not continuous, but the trend survives the gaps. A record kept for another purpose has become evidence for a changing climate.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To compare two lakes and explain their differences.
To describe the physics of lake freezing in detail.
To argue that the monastery records are useless.
To show how an incidental historical record can document long-term change.

questions.explanation: The final sentence states the reinterpretation of an old record.

distractor_rationales.B: The physics is not the subject.
distractor_rationales.C: The records are presented as valuable.
distractor_rationales.A: Only one lake is discussed.

questions.stimulus: A chef testing a new oven found that the same recipe produced different results on different shelves. The top shelf browned too quickly, the bottom stayed pale. The chef rotated the trays halfway through and the variation fell. The oven's heat was uneven, and the method had been hiding it.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It argues that oven shelves make no difference.
It lists the ingredients of the recipe.
It compares two ovens made by different manufacturers.
It reports observations, describes a fix, and explains what the observations revealed.

questions.explanation: Observation, remedy and diagnosis form the sequence.

distractor_rationales.A: Shelf position is the variable.
distractor_rationales.B: Ingredients are not listed.
distractor_rationales.C: One oven is tested.

questions.stimulus: Some desert plants open their pores at night rather than during the day. The cooler air reduces water loss, and the plant stores the carbon it takes in until daylight. The strategy trades a slower process for a much smaller water bill, which matters where rain is rare.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To compare desert plants with rainforest species.
To explain how a night-time strategy reduces water loss in dry conditions.
To argue that opening pores at midday is more efficient.
To describe how desert plants store water in their leaves.

questions.explanation: The passage links timing, temperature and water loss.

distractor_rationales.D: Storage of water is not described.
distractor_rationales.C: Midday opening would increase loss.
distractor_rationales.A: No rainforest comparison appears.

questions.stimulus: A clockmaker adjusts a pendulum's length to change its period. A longer pendulum swings more slowly; a shorter one swings faster. Temperature matters too, because metal expands in warmth. Precision clocks therefore use alloys that change little with heat, or compensate with a second metal that expands in the opposite direction.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It states a basic relationship, introduces a complication, and describes two responses to it.
It argues that temperature has no effect on clocks.
It narrates the invention of the pendulum clock.
It lists the parts of a clock in the order they are assembled.

questions.explanation: The period-length relation, thermal expansion, and two compensations build the paragraph.

distractor_rationales.C: No invention narrative appears.
distractor_rationales.B: Temperature is the complication.
distractor_rationales.D: No assembly order is given.

questions.stimulus: A farmer plants a cover crop after harvest. The roots hold soil through winter rains, and the plants add organic matter when they are turned in. The field looks idle, but the cover crop is working. Yield in the following season often rises even though nothing was harvested in between.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To explain the unseen benefits of a crop grown between harvests.
To describe how to harvest a cover crop for profit.
To argue that bare soil is better for yields.

questions.explanation: The passage explains what the cover crop does while looking idle.

distractor_rationales.B: Nothing is harvested from the cover crop.
distractor_rationales.D: Bare soil is the contrast case.
distractor_rationales.C: No brands are compared.

questions.stimulus: The first tests of a new vaccine measure immune response, not protection. A later trial follows thousands of people to see who becomes ill. The two stages answer different questions, and a strong immune response in the first does not guarantee success in the second. Reading the first result as a verdict is a common error.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It reports the results of a completed field trial.
It distinguishes two stages, explains what each measures, and warns against conflating them.
It argues that early trials are unnecessary.
It describes the manufacturing process of a vaccine.

questions.explanation: The paragraph separates the two questions and names the mistake of merging them.

distractor_rationales.D: Manufacturing is not described.
distractor_rationales.C: Early trials are presented as one stage.
distractor_rationales.A: No results are reported.

questions.stimulus: A stone arch bridge carries load by compression. Each block pushes against its neighbors, and the curve directs the force into the abutments. The bridge can stand for centuries because the material is strong in compression. It fails when water scours the foundation and the abutments move, not because the stone crumbles.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It compares stone and steel bridges and prefers steel.
It argues that arches carry load in tension.
It explains the structural principle and then names the usual cause of failure.
It describes the construction sequence of a bridge.

questions.explanation: The principle of compression is followed by scour as the failure mode.

distractor_rationales.A: No steel comparison appears.
distractor_rationales.D: Construction order is not given.
distractor_rationales.B: The passage specifies compression.

questions.stimulus: An archive received a box of letters with no catalog. A conservator noted the paper, ink and postmarks before anyone read them. The postmarks placed the letters in three decades; the ink identified two writers. Reading came last, after the physical evidence had narrowed the possibilities.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It describes how paper is manufactured.
It argues that letters should be read before being examined.
It lists the contents of the box in detail.
It narrates a sequence in which physical analysis precedes reading.

questions.explanation: The order of steps is the structure the question asks about.

distractor_rationales.B: Reading comes last in the passage.
distractor_rationales.C: Contents are summarized, not listed.
distractor_rationales.A: Manufacture is not discussed.

questions.stimulus: A tidal flat looks uniform from a distance. Up close it holds channels, pools and patches of mud of different grain sizes. Each patch drains at a different rate, so the animals living in them experience different periods of exposure. A single square meter can contain several distinct habitats.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To list the species found on tidal flats.
To show how small-scale variation creates distinct habitats on a seemingly uniform flat.
To describe the tides that cover a flat twice a day.
To argue that grain size has no effect on drainage.

questions.explanation: The contrast between distant and close views carries the point.

distractor_rationales.C: Tide timing is not the subject.
distractor_rationales.D: Grain size is tied to drainage.
distractor_rationales.A: Species are mentioned generally.

questions.stimulus: A baker's starter failed after a move to a new city. The flour was different, and so was the water. Replacing the flour restored the rise within a week, which suggested that the water was not the problem. The starter had been selective about its food all along.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It describes a problem, tests one cause, and draws a conclusion from the result.
It compares two cities and their baking traditions.
It argues that water quality never affects baking.
It lists the steps for making a starter from scratch.

questions.explanation: The flour swap isolates the cause and produces the conclusion.

distractor_rationales.B: No traditions are compared.
distractor_rationales.C: Water is ruled out only after the flour test.
distractor_rationales.D: No recipe is given.

questions.stimulus: A lighthouse's beam is narrow because a wide beam spreads its light too thin to be seen far. Rotating the beam sweeps the horizon, so a distant ship sees a flash rather than a steady glow. The flash pattern identifies the lighthouse, which is why each station has a different interval.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It argues that a wide beam is easier to see at sea.
It explains a design choice, describes its effect, and states a further function of that effect.
It narrates the construction of a lighthouse tower.
It compares two lighthouses of different heights.

questions.explanation: Narrow beam, rotation and identifying flash build on one another.

distractor_rationales.C: Construction is not described.
distractor_rationales.A: A wide beam spreads light too thin.
distractor_rationales.D: Heights are not compared.

questions.stimulus: A museum once displayed a bronze horse without its stand because the stand was thought to be a later addition. Analysis of the metal showed the stand and the horse were cast together. The display was changed, and the label now explains that the two parts belong to one object.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To argue that museum labels are never revised.
To show how material analysis corrected an assumption about an object's parts.
To describe the process of casting bronze.
To compare two bronze horses from different museums.

questions.explanation: The passage contrasts an old assumption with the analysis that overturned it.

distractor_rationales.C: Casting technique is not explained.
distractor_rationales.A: A revision is the subject.
distractor_rationales.D: One object is discussed.

questions.stimulus: A floodplain is not wasted land. When a river overtops its banks, the water slows and drops sediment that renews the soil. The same flood that damages a road may improve a field. Building levees everywhere removes the benefit along with the risk, which is why some rivers are now reconnected to their floodplains.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It lists the costs of flooding without mentioning benefits.
It describes the geology of a river delta.
It argues that levees are the only sensible flood policy.
It challenges a common view, explains a benefit, and describes a policy response.

questions.explanation: The opening reframing leads to the sediment benefit and the reconnection policy.

distractor_rationales.C: Levees are presented as removing a benefit.
distractor_rationales.B: Delta geology is not described.
distractor_rationales.A: Benefits are central to the passage.

questions.stimulus: A new telescope's mirror is made of many hexagonal segments. Each segment is adjusted by actuators so that the whole surface behaves as one curve. A single large mirror would be too heavy to launch, so the design trades complexity on the ground for a lighter payload in orbit.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It describes the launch sequence of a rocket.
It explains a design, describes how it works, and states the trade-off that motivated it.
It argues that a single large mirror is easier to launch.
It compares the images from two telescopes.

questions.explanation: Segment design, actuation and the launch-weight trade-off structure the passage.

distractor_rationales.A: No launch sequence appears.
distractor_rationales.C: A single mirror is too heavy.
distractor_rationales.D: No images are compared.

questions.stimulus: A seed catalog lists a tomato as resistant to a disease. Resistance does not mean immunity: the plant may still show symptoms under heavy pressure. Gardeners who read the label as a guarantee are disappointed, though the variety may still outperform others in the same bed.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To argue that resistant varieties never show symptoms.
To compare two tomato varieties for flavour.
To clarify a term that is easily misread as a stronger promise than it is.
To describe how to grow tomatoes from seed.

questions.explanation: The passage defines resistance against a common misreading.

distractor_rationales.D: Growing instructions are absent.
distractor_rationales.A: Symptoms can still appear.
distractor_rationales.B: Flavour is not discussed.

questions.stimulus: A choral conductor asks singers to breathe in the same place in a phrase. The instruction is not about stamina. A shared breath makes the consonants land together, which is what the audience hears as precision. The technique is therefore about ensemble rather than endurance.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It states an instruction, rejects an obvious explanation, and gives the real one.
It explains how to train a solo voice.
It argues that singers should breathe whenever they choose.
It describes the history of choral music.

questions.explanation: The passage moves from instruction to rejected reason to the ensemble explanation.

distractor_rationales.D: No history is given.
distractor_rationales.C: Shared breathing is the instruction.
distractor_rationales.B: The focus is ensemble, not solo training.

questions.stimulus: A concrete path cracks because it is restrained at the edges while the slab expands in heat. The crack relieves the stress at one point but concentrates it at the ends. A line of joints cut across the path gives the concrete places to move, so the cracks form where they were planned instead of randomly.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It explains a failure, describes how it propagates, and presents a design that controls it.
It describes the mixing of a concrete batch.
It compares two kinds of concrete and ranks their strength.
It argues that joints make cracking worse.

questions.explanation: Cause, propagation and control joints form the sequence.

distractor_rationales.C: No strength ranking appears.
distractor_rationales.D: Joints control where cracks form.
distractor_rationales.B: Mixing is not discussed.

questions.stimulus: A historian reading a merchant's ledger noticed that the same cargo was recorded twice, once on departure and once on arrival. The two entries differ by a small amount, which probably reflects loss in transit. Such gaps, collected across many voyages, can estimate how much cargo never reached port.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It compares two merchants and their profits.
It argues that ledgers are too unreliable to use.
It narrates a single voyage from departure to arrival.
It describes a detail in a source and explains how that detail can be used at scale.

questions.explanation: A small discrepancy becomes a method when aggregated over many records.

distractor_rationales.C: No voyage narrative is given.
distractor_rationales.B: The ledger is used, not dismissed.
distractor_rationales.A: One merchant is discussed.

questions.stimulus: Some spiders build webs that reflect ultraviolet light. Insects see ultraviolet, so the web appears as a bright pattern to them while remaining nearly invisible to birds that might tear through it. The silk is not decorative; it is tuned to the vision of a particular audience.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To explain how a web's appearance is shaped by the vision of different animals.
To describe how spiders spin silk threads.
To argue that birds are attracted to ultraviolet webs.
To compare the strength of two kinds of spider silk.

questions.explanation: The UV reflection is explained by what insects and birds can see.

distractor_rationales.B: Spinning is not described.
distractor_rationales.C: Birds see the web as nearly invisible.
distractor_rationales.D: Strength is not compared.

questions.stimulus: A town's water supply came from a spring above the town. The pipe ran downhill, so no pump was needed, but the pressure at the top of the hill was too low for firefighting. A second tank halfway up solved the problem by holding water at a height that gave pressure without a pump.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It argues that pumps are always necessary.
It describes a system, names a shortcoming, and explains the remedy.
It compares two towns and their water supplies.
It describes the construction of a spring house.

questions.explanation: Gravity feed, weak pressure uphill, and a mid-level tank form the sequence.

distractor_rationales.C: One town is discussed.
distractor_rationales.A: The solutions avoid pumps.
distractor_rationales.D: No spring house is described.

questions.stimulus: A paper was retracted after readers found that two figures were identical. The authors said the duplication was an error in assembling the manuscript. The journal's notice did not decide intent, only that the published record could no longer be relied on. Correction and misconduct are separate questions.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It argues that every retraction proves misconduct.
It compares two journals and their retraction policies.
It describes how to assemble figures for publication.
It reports an event, notes the authors' explanation, and distinguishes two issues the notice leaves separate.

questions.explanation: The final sentence draws the distinction the notice preserves.

distractor_rationales.A: The passage separates correction from misconduct.
distractor_rationales.C: Figure assembly is mentioned but not explained.
distractor_rationales.B: One journal is discussed.

questions.stimulus: A beekeeper inspects a hive less often in winter. Opening the hive releases heat the colony has stored, and the bees must spend energy replacing it. A quick check may cost less than a cold night. The timing of an inspection is therefore a calculation, not a habit.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It describes a practice and explains the cost that justifies it.
It compares two species of bee.
It argues that hives should be opened daily in winter.
It describes how bees make honey.

questions.explanation: The heat cost explains why inspections are rationed.

distractor_rationales.D: Honey making is not described.
distractor_rationales.C: The passage recommends less frequent inspection.
distractor_rationales.B: One species is discussed.

questions.stimulus: A geologist found shells on a mountain top. The shells are marine, and the rock around them formed under water. The explanation is not that the sea once reached this height, but that the rock was lifted. Uplift is slow, which is why the shells remain intact rather than being crushed.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It argues that the shells were carried up by birds.
It narrates a climb to a mountain summit.
It poses an observation, rejects one explanation, and supplies another with supporting detail.

questions.explanation: The observation, rejected sea-level explanation and uplift account form the structure.

distractor_rationales.C: No climb is described.
distractor_rationales.B: Birds are not mentioned.
distractor_rationales.A: One location is discussed.

questions.stimulus: A violin maker chooses wood for how it rings when tapped. A plate that rings too long sounds hollow under the bow; one that dies quickly sounds thin. The maker removes wood from the edges until the tap tone falls into a range learned from experience rather than measured on a scale.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To argue that tap tone is irrelevant to violin sound.
To explain a judgement made by ear rather than by measurement.
To describe the chemical treatment of violin varnish.
To compare two famous violin makers.

questions.explanation: The passage contrasts an experienced ear with a measured scale.

distractor_rationales.C: Varnish is not discussed.
distractor_rationales.A: Tap tone is central.
distractor_rationales.D: No makers are compared.

questions.stimulus: A long drought exposed a submerged bridge in a reservoir. The bridge was built before the valley was flooded and had been underwater for sixty years. Its piers were intact, but the deck had sagged where water had entered the joints. The reservoir's low level turned a hidden structure into a visible record of its own construction.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It argues that the bridge should never have been flooded.
It lists the materials used in bridge piers.
It begins with a chance event and uses it to describe what the revealed structure shows.
It describes the engineering of reservoir dams.

questions.explanation: The drought is the occasion; the bridge's condition is the content.

distractor_rationales.A: No judgement about flooding is offered.
distractor_rationales.D: Dams are not described.
distractor_rationales.B: Materials are not listed.

questions.stimulus: A museum's textile gallery dims its lights. Dyes fade in proportion to the light they receive, and a year of bright display can do more damage than a century in a drawer. Visitors sometimes complain about the gloom, but the alternative is the gradual disappearance of the objects they came to see.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It argues that bright lighting preserves textiles.
It compares two museums and their visitor numbers.
It explains a policy, gives its rationale, and acknowledges a cost.
It describes the manufacture of natural dyes.

questions.explanation: Dim lighting, the fading mechanism and the visitor complaint complete the structure.

distractor_rationales.A: Light causes fading.
distractor_rationales.D: Dye manufacture is not described.
distractor_rationales.B: Visitor numbers are not compared.

questions.stimulus: A new bridge was built beside the old one rather than on its site. Keeping the old bridge open during construction meant traffic never stopped, but it also meant the new structure had to fit a narrower corridor. The builders accepted the constraint because the alternative was months of closure.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It describes a decision and explains the trade-off that justified it.
It compares the cost of two bridges in detail.
It narrates the failure of the old bridge.
It argues that road closures are always preferable.

questions.explanation: The siting decision and its traffic trade-off are the passage's content.

distractor_rationales.B: No cost figures are given.
distractor_rationales.C: The old bridge stayed open.
distractor_rationales.D: Closures are the alternative that was avoided.

questions.stimulus: A seed's size limits how far the wind can carry it. Small, winged seeds travel far but carry little stored food, so a seedling must establish quickly. Large seeds land near the parent but have reserves to survive shade. The trade-off shapes which species colonise open ground and which persist in closed forest.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It states a constraint, contrasts two strategies, and draws a consequence for where species grow.
It argues that large seeds travel farther than small ones.
It lists the animals that disperse seeds.
It describes the anatomy of a seed in detail.

questions.explanation: Size, dispersal and establishment lead to the habitat conclusion.

distractor_rationales.D: Anatomy is not the subject.
distractor_rationales.B: Small winged seeds travel farther.
distractor_rationales.C: No animals are listed.

questions.stimulus: An archaeologist found a hearth with ash, burnt bone and a ring of stones. The stones were not local. Analysis matched them to a riverbed two days' walk away. The hearth therefore records not only a fire but a decision to carry heavy material to a place where it was wanted.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It narrates a journey to a riverbed.
It compares two hearths from different sites.
It presents evidence, links it to a distant source, and infers deliberate behavior.
It argues that the stones arrived by natural transport.

questions.explanation: Evidence, provenance and inference about effort form the structure.

distractor_rationales.A: The journey is inferred, not narrated.
distractor_rationales.D: The analysis ties the stones to the riverbed.
distractor_rationales.B: One hearth is discussed.

questions.stimulus: A textile printer tests a dye on a scrap before committing a whole bolt. The scrap is washed, dried and exposed to light in conditions harsher than ordinary use. If the color survives that, the bolt is printed. The test is a small, deliberate failure used to prevent a large one.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To explain why a small destructive test protects a larger investment.
To argue that testing scraps is a waste of material.
To describe how dye is extracted from plants.

questions.explanation: The last sentence states the logic of the sample test.

distractor_rationales.C: Extraction is not described.
distractor_rationales.B: The test prevents loss.
distractor_rationales.D: No machines are compared.

questions.stimulus: A city planted trees along a new road. Within five years, half had died, mostly in the pits cut into compacted ground. The failures were not caused by drought or disease but by roots unable to spread beyond the pit. Later plantings broke the surrounding compaction before planting.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It reports an outcome, rules out two explanations, and identifies the real cause.
It narrates the construction of the road.
It lists the species of trees planted.
It argues that tree pits are the best place to plant.

questions.explanation: Mortality, rejected causes and compaction form the paragraph.

distractor_rationales.B: Road construction is incidental.
distractor_rationales.D: Pits are the problem.
distractor_rationales.C: Species are not listed.

questions.stimulus: A stone tool's edge dulls at a rate that depends on what it cuts. Microscopic wear on a blade can distinguish hide from wood from bone. An archaeologist can therefore infer what a tool was used for without finding the material it worked on. The evidence is the surface, not the residue.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To argue that tools cannot reveal their function.
To describe how stone tools are made.
To explain how wear patterns on a tool reveal its past use.

questions.explanation: The passage explains wear analysis and its inferential reach.

distractor_rationales.C: Manufacture is not described.
distractor_rationales.B: Function is the subject.
distractor_rationales.A: No sites are compared.

questions.stimulus: A wick must be the right size for a candle. Too small and the flame starves; too large and it smokes, leaving soot on the glass. Candle makers match wick diameter to the wax and the container. A wick that works in one candle may fail in another of the same height.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It narrates the history of candle making.
It argues that one wick size suits every candle.
It describes a requirement, gives failure modes, and concludes that the choice is specific.
It describes how wax is refined.

questions.explanation: Requirement, failure modes and the specificity conclusion build the text.

distractor_rationales.A: No history is given.
